# Phase 8, Step 3: MCQ expansion from 240 toward 300

**66 new original questions** in 11 unpublished draft sets (`content/drafts/mcq-expansion/XQ-01..XQ-11`, generated by `build_mcqs.py`), bringing the draft bank to **306** (240 + 66). All are DRAFT, `clinically_reviewed: false`, and are not importable: the question bank holds only synthetic fixtures and no import path exists for these files (unit-tested).

| Set | Topic (skill / medication drafts) | Main sources (full text read) |
|---|---|---|
| XQ-01 | Urinary catheter care (SK-12) | CDC CAUTI guideline 2009 |
| XQ-02 | Peripheral IV care (SK-03) | CDC catheter guideline 2011 |
| XQ-03 | Central venous catheter care (SK-02) | CDC 2011; SHEA 2022 |
| XQ-04 | Patient transfer (SK-20) | ICS transfer guidance 2026 |
| XQ-05 | Chest drain monitoring (SK-13) | BTS clinical statement 2023 |
| XQ-06 | Safe mobilization (SK-16) | Hodgson 2014 consensus |
| XQ-07 | CRRT alarms and prescription checks (SK-17) | AHS CRRT alarm pathway 2025; KDIGO 2012 |
| XQ-08 | Vasoactive medication safety (MD-01..05) | FDA labels (norepinephrine, epinephrine, vasopressin, dobutamine, milrinone) |
| XQ-09 | Sedative and opioid safety (MD-06..10) | FDA labels (propofol, midazolam, dexmedetomidine, fentanyl, morphine) |
| XQ-10 | Nasogastric tube position (SK-10, SK-11) | NICE CG32; NHS 2016 alert |
| XQ-11 | Scope of practice and escalation across skills | the sources above |

**Coverage rule applied:** questions were written only where a statement in a source read in full supports one defensible answer. Nothing was written for tracheostomy care (still unsupported) and no question depends on a dose, rate, concentration or titration. Each question has plausible distractors with a one-line reason each, a "why correct" explanation and a **Trace** line naming the registered source(s) and the statement it rests on.

## Checks (reusing the existing draft validator and audit)
* `npm run validate:mcq` (`scripts/validate-mcq-expansion.ts`): front matter, banner, structure and quality rules of `src/lib/draft-validator.ts` (four options, one key, per-option explanation, distractor plausibility, per-set position and length balance), trace sources must exist in the registers, no dose pattern, no review claim, references with access dates, answer positions balanced across the expansion (A/B/C/D = 16/16/17/17), no near-duplicate (Jaccard 0.5 or more) among the new questions or against the 240 existing ones. Result: **0 issues**.
* `scripts/audit-mcqs.ts` now audits all 306 questions together (`content/drafts/MCQ_AUDIT.md`): positions 75/79/77/75; correct option unique longest 76 (24.8%) and unique shortest 75 (24.5%), both within the expected range for a random key; no identical options; no near-duplicates (0.7); 132 questions carry at least one advisory flag (94 of the original 240; 38 of the 66 new ones, mostly the key being the longest or a stem without a clinical cue). Flags are advisory and are left for the review phase.
* Unit tests (`tests/unit/mcq-expansion.test.ts`, 6) cover the positive checks and the negative cases (review claim, missing/unknown trace, dose content, weak distractor, unbalanced key).

## Limits
Questions are original paraphrases of US, UK and Canadian sources; jurisdiction differs by item and is noted in the traces. Medication questions rest on US FDA labels only. Difficulty has not been calibrated and no question has had a clinical or language review; the key is the author's reading of the source. Advisory flags (item-writing cues) should be cleared during review.
